node_definition.done_when: Read section 25 of crew-observability-truth first. First show the defect still reproduces at your base: crew ack for a promoted run whose worktree is still held refuses with "no live run" (record_run_acknowledgement in reckon/crew/runs.py). Then a deliberate remainder of a promoted run, worktree-held or another duty the obligations reader raises from the run's ledger record, can be acknowledged with a reason and an expiry. The acknowledgement is stored somewhere a promoted run can own; the live pointer is gone by then, so it cannot live there. reckon/crew/obligations.py honours it exactly as it honours a live run's acknowledgement today, through _acknowledgements_in_force and _partition_acknowledged. An acknowledgement with no reason is refused. tests/test_ack_after_promotion.py promotes a run whose worktree is still held and acknowledges it with a reason. It asserts the obligation leaves the stop path, returns when the acknowledgement expires, and that an acknowledgement with no reason is refused. Every case works in a temporary config home and repository. The first case fails at your base. Existing tests reaching crew ack, record_run_acknowledgement and the acknowledgement readers keep passing; grep tests/ for each to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/ack-after-promotion.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
